scenarios.name: update-type-overdraft-rate
scenarios.why: SELECT +0, valid type: UPDATE sets type, overdraft and rate; the COMMAREA refilled from the host variables, the dates reformatted from Db2's ISO text; 'Y'

scenarios.name: update-negative-balance-account
scenarios.why: a negative DECIMAL(12,2) balance into COMM-AVAIL-BAL / COMM-ACTUAL-BAL (S9(10)V99)

scenarios.name: update-max-values
scenarios.why: COMM-OVERDRAFT 99999999 into INTEGER, COMM-INT-RATE 9999.99 into DECIMAL(6,2) (the largest each PICTURE holds); balance 9999999999.99

scenarios.name: leap-day-opened
scenarios.why: an account opened 2024-02-29: the date's parts moved by position

scenarios.name: account-not-found
scenarios.why: SELECT INTO no row: SQLCODE +100, 'N', no UPDATE

scenarios.name: other-sort-code-not-found
scenarios.why: COMM-SCODE is overwritten by the program's own SORTCODE (987654): account 123456/00000001 is never read, 987654/00000001 is

scenarios.name: blank-account-type
scenarios.why: type all spaces: 'N' after the SELECT, no UPDATE

scenarios.name: type-starts-with-space
scenarios.why: type's first byte a space: 'N', no UPDATE

scenarios.name: null-statement-date
scenarios.why: ACCOUNT_LAST_STATEMENT is NULL and its host variable has no indicator: SELECT INTO is SQLCODE -305, 'N', no UPDATE

scenarios.name: mortgage-update
scenarios.why: a second successful update, a large negative balance

scenarios.name: eibcalen-full
scenarios.why: the whole 99-byte COMMAREA passed: EIBCALEN equals the record, nothing past it

scenarios.name: foreign-sort-code-blank-type
scenarios.why: a failing run ('N', blank type) with a caller sort code other than the program's: MOVE SORTCODE TO COMM-SCODE is the only write, so the returned COMM-SCODE shows it (the success path rewrites it from the host variable)

scenarios.name: eyecatcher-refilled-from-db
scenarios.why: the caller's COMM-EYE differs from the row's ACCOUNT_EYECATCHER: the success path's MOVE HV-ACCOUNT-EYECATCHER TO COMM-EYE is the only thing that makes the returned eyecatcher the row's

scenarios.name: dto-entry-update
scenarios.why: as update-type-overdraft-rate, through the typed DTO alone (#4049): the link-area bytes no longer overwrite what in_ maps, so each COMM-* field's move from the DTO shows in the UPDATE and the refilled COMMAREA

scenarios.name: dto-entry-account-not-found
scenarios.why: as account-not-found, through the typed DTO alone (#4049): a failing run returns the caller's DTO fields as in_ mapped them

scenarios.name: dto-entry-eibcalen-full
scenarios.why: as eibcalen-full (99 bytes), through the typed DTO alone (#4049)

scenarios.name: dto-entry-foreign-sort-code
scenarios.why: as foreign-sort-code-blank-type, through the typed DTO alone (#4049): in_ maps COMM-SCODE and COMM-EYE, the failing path returns them

scenarios.name: dto-entry-eyecatcher
scenarios.why: as eyecatcher-refilled-from-db, through the typed DTO alone (#4049)

scenarios.name: dto-entry-caller-fields-kept-on-failure
scenarios.why: a failing run (account 99 not found) through the typed DTO alone, with every COMM-* field the caller sends non-blank / non-zero: the program writes only SCODE and SUCCESS on this path, so the returned COMMAREA shows each other field exactly as in_ mapped it (#4049; the field-by-field moves and widths at the DTO entry)

scenarios.name: null-eyecatcher
scenarios.why: the row's only NULL is ACCOUNT_EYECATCHER (every other column set) and its host variable has no indicator: SELECT INTO is SQLCODE -305, 'N', no UPDATE. Each column of the null test is judged alone, so a mutant that joins two of them with && instead of || cannot hide behind ACCOUNT_LAST_STATEMENT (#4049)

notes: CBSA's update-account service (UPDACC, LINKed with the UPDACC copybook's COMMAREA): the account is read by the program's own sort code (987654) and COMM-ACCNO with a SELECT INTO from Db2 table ACCOUNT (unqualified: the bind's QUALIFIER, IBMUSER); a failed SELECT (+100, -305 ...) or an account type that is blank or starts with a space gives COMM-SUCCESS 'N' and no UPDATE; otherwise ACCOUNT_TYPE, ACCOUNT_INTEREST_RATE and ACCOUNT_OVERDRAFT_LIMIT are UPDATEd, and the COMMAREA is refilled from the host variables, each date reformatted from Db2's character form (YYYY-MM-DD) to DDMMYYYY. The table is compared after every scenario.
